## Dispatching — `domain:ui` execution seat, 2026-09-14T21:09Z

Claimed: `os-dev` seat, by the `domain:ui` execution seat (`os-tesla`).

Session: session_011QreXiyMEqKLN4U5daMPVa

Clause-②: yes

**Clause-② `yes`** on the "not sure ⇒ yes" rule. The deliverable below is an instrument plus a gate and should touch no published declaration — but whether the ledger file it produces is itself governed surface is not knowable before the work, and this seat would rather run a review it did not owe than skip one it did.

### Graded `priority:p2`

⛔ Not p3: this card **blocks** objectui#9256. That card's family-D narrowing held out **eleven** registrations, and **nine of them are held for exactly this question** — *"which declaration governs a bare name is unmeasured"*. It is also the stated reason `sidebar` was held out of family B back in PR objectui#9254. ⇒ two cards are parked on one unmeasured fact.

⛔ Not p1: nothing is broken today that anyone has reported. The symptom is latent — *"the wrong renderer, chosen by import order, for a node that type-checks fine."*

---

## ⭐⭐ Correction to the card, and it changes the job

**The card says the repo carries "two ad-hoc mitigations". It carries at least eight artefacts, and one of them is most of your instrument.** This seat re-derived the surface at `origin/main` `bbc9dc3` before writing this. ⛔ Do not start from the card's picture — start from this one.

**⭐ The instrument already exists.** `scripts/unit-registry-collision.mjs:262` — `readOwnRegistrations(sourceText, fileName)` walks the TS AST for `ComponentRegistry.register` / `.registerLazy` calls and already resolves the type expression, the `namespace`, and `skipFallback` — and **already emits the bare key precisely when `!skipFallback`**:

```js
if (namespace) {
  keys.push(`${namespace}:${type}`);
  if (!skipFallback) keys.push(type);       // ← the bare-name claim, already derived
} else { keys.push(type); }
```

It also reports **unresolved** key expressions rather than dropping them, and it already ships `findCollisions`, `formatCollisions`, `resolveSpecifier`, `collectFiles`, and a `FLOORS` / `checkFloors` non-vacuity pair (`:337`). ⚠️ It is scoped to the vitest `unit` project (`unitProjectFiles`) and aimed at a **different** question (objectui#7134 — `isolate: false` safety). ⇒ your job on this half is **widen the population and re-aim the grouping**, ⛔ not write a second AST walker.

**⚠️ A runtime collision guard already exists too — the card does not mention it.** `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts:491-503`:

> `Component "${type}" bare-name fallback is being overwritten by "${fullType}".`

⇒ *"nothing surfaces a collision"* is **false at runtime**. The card's real claim survives, and it is narrower and sharper: **nothing FAILS.** A `console.warn` in a browser console is not a gate.

**⚠️ And the guard is asymmetric.** `register()` has it; **`registerLazy()` at `:559-567` does not** — it takes the same `meta?.namespace && !meta?.skipFallback` branch and writes the bare key with **no collision check at all**. ⭐ That matters more than it looks: `apps/console` registers its plugin stubs through `registerLazy`, so the phase-dependent double-claim that objectui#6416 is entirely about goes through the **unguarded** door. ⛔ Verify this yourself before relying on it.

**Prior art you must read before designing anything** — these establish the technique and the vocabulary; ⛔ do not duplicate them:

| artefact | what it already pins |
|---|---|
| `packages/plugin-report/src/__tests__/report-bare-key-ownership.test.ts` | ⭐ the **replay-in-both-orders** technique: re-registers the package's REAL declared metadata into a fresh `Registry` alongside a console-shaped lazy stub, **in both orders**, checking the bare key after EVERY step. Its own docblock says why: *"asserting only today's resolved outcome cannot tell 'declared' apart from 'happened to be observed after the right step'."* |
| `packages/plugin-timeline/src/__tests__/timeline-bare-key-ownership.test.ts` | the same shape, second package |
| `packages/fields/src/__tests__/registry-collision.test.ts` | `FIELD_TYPES_SKIP_FALLBACK` — five names (`text`, `image`, `avatar`, `html`, `grid`) resolved by *deliberate* `skipFallback`. ⚠️ **These are collisions that are already correctly handled** — your ledger must be able to say so, or it will report five false alarms |
| `scripts/__tests__/report-namespace-agreement-6416.test.ts` | cross-site derivation (package ↔ console stub ↔ CLI whitelist) |
| `packages/core/src/registry/public-blocks.ts:47` | the `record:line_items` case-by-case workaround (the one mitigation the card did name) |

---

## The deliverable

**Two things, in this order. ⛔ The second does not begin until the first is on the card.**

### ① Re-derive the population, and post the table on this card before any gate is written

⚠️ **The card's own counts are declared unverified by the seat that filed them**, and it says so in as many words:

> a repair round must re-run the enumeration against a BUILT tree and name each of the 19 individually before acting. Both instrument defects answered **wrong silently**, so an unreplicated count from that run is a lead, not a result.

⇒ **19 names and "eight cross-package" are LEADS. Treat any number you inherit as unmeasured.** The two defects that answered wrong silently in the originating run are documented in objectui#9256's table comment — read them and prove your instrument is free of both:

1. **bare type-NAME attribution** pooled `__type` / `Record` across unrelated inline types;
2. **an unbuilt tree resolves `@object-ui/types` to `any`**, and `any` reads as "reads neither".

⇒ build the tree first, and carry a **module-resolution probe** reporting unresolved-module diagnostics, as PR objectui#9261 did.

**Name every collision individually**: the bare key, each claimant (package, file, line, full namespaced type), whether each passes `skipFallback`, and whether the claim is via `register` or `registerLazy`. ⭐ A count is not a result here — the nine hold-outs on objectui#9256 need to be resolvable **one at a time**, and a bare integer resolves none of them.

**Lit controls are mandatory, both directions.** ⛔ A zero from a sweep with no live control is not a reading. At minimum: the five deliberate `skipFallback` names from `registry-collision.test.ts` must appear as *handled*, and `record:line_items` must appear as *handled* — if your instrument cannot see the cases the repo already solved, it cannot be trusted about the ones it hasn't.

### ② The gate

A repo-wide check that **FAILS** when a new bare-name collision lands, with the measured set as a **shrink-only ledger** — the same technique this repo uses in `DEBT` blocks and in `check-entry-guard`'s `KNOWN_HAND_TYPED_GUARDS`. Entries carry the claimants, not just the name. Follow `unit-registry-collision.mjs`'s `FLOORS` / `checkFloors` so a sweep that silently stops finding anything is non-vacuous by construction.

Prove it with an **ablation**: predict the direction in writing first, then introduce a bare-name collision on disk (prove the mutation landed by anchor count **and** blob hash), show the gate RED naming the new collision, restore, and prove the restore **by state** — `git diff HEAD` empty **and** a matching blob hash.

---

## ⛔ Out of scope — do not do these

- ⛔ **Do not add `skipFallback: true` to any registration to "fix" a collision.** That changes which renderer a bare name resolves to. It is a **behaviour change per collision**, each needs its own ruling, and objectui#9256's nine hold-outs are held precisely because nobody has made those rulings. Your deliverable makes them **decidable**; it does not decide them.
- ⛔ **Do not make `register()` throw.** Turning today's warn into a failure is the same behaviour change wearing a gate's clothes. The gate belongs in CI, not in the runtime path.
- ⛔ **Do not narrow any objectui#9256 hold-out**, even if your measurement makes one look obvious. That card is open and this is its blocker, not its successor.
- ⛔ **Do not repurpose `scripts/unit-registry-collision.mjs`'s existing exports out from under objectui#7134's gate.** `scripts/__tests__/unit-registry-absence-collision.test.ts` imports eleven of them by name. Extend additively, or factor the shared walker out with both callers passing their own population — ⛔ never change an existing export's meaning.
- ⛔ Families C and E (objectui#9256's out-of-scope list) stay frozen.

---

## Gates this diff's shape owes

⚠️ Hand-derived from **objectui's own** workflows at `bbc9dc3` — `dispatch-gates.mjs` lives in the `objectstack` tree and **refuses** to answer about this repo (it did, when asked; the refusal is the correct behaviour and its answer would have been about the wrong board). ⇒ treat this list as a floor, not a ceiling, and run what your actual diff touches.

A new `scripts/*.mjs` entry point owes, at minimum:

- **`check-entry-guard.mjs`** (runs in `lint.yml` *and* `changeset-guard.yml`) — ⚠️ **this is the one that reddened PR objectui#9238 in CI after passing locally.** Use `isEntrypoint(import.meta.url)` from `scripts/invoked-as.mjs`. ⛔ A hand-typed `process.argv[1]` comparison is the single spelling this repo forbids, and it fails in the worst direction: through a symlink it answers `false`, the gate does nothing, and **exit 0 with no output is indistinguishable from a pass**.
- **`check-node-esm-load.mjs`** (`node-esm-load-gate.yml`), **`check-control-bytes`** + **`check-test-path-roots`** (`lint.yml`), **`check-new-cross-file-line-citations`** (`line-citation-gate.yml`) — ⭐ this last one matters here, because everything above cites `file:line` across files.
- The changeset family (`changeset-presence` / `-no-major` / `-fixed` / `-overwrite` / `-claims`). ⚠️ A test file under `src/` of a released package counts as published source by `check-changeset-presence`'s own criterion **even when nothing ships** — the answer is an **empty-frontmatter** changeset declaring no release, ⛔ never an exemption.
- If you touch `packages/core/**`: **Bundle Analysis** (`performance-budget.yml`) and **Type Check**.
- If you edit a README fence or an `@example`: the two doc-snippet gates. ⚠️ Both compile against **built** `dist/*.d.ts`; an unbuilt tree answers `exit 2 [unbuilt-package]`, which is **PREREQUISITE NOT MET** — ⛔ not a pass and ⛔ not a red.

Run heavy work through `/home/user/objectstack/scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`. Capture exit codes by **redirect-then-capture**, ⛔ never through a pipe.

Branch `claude/issue-9264-bare-name-collision-gate`, base `bbc9dc3`, measured after
`turbo run build` (44 of 44 build tasks green, 39 `dist/` directories present).

⛔ **Every figure the card and objectui#9256 carried is treated as a LEAD here.** The
instrument below reproduces none of them: the 19 names are resolved one at a time and
sixteen of them turn out not to be collisions at all, while the one key that IS contested
appears on neither list.

---

### The instrument

`node scripts/check-registry-bare-name-collisions.mjs --table` (also `--json`). It is the
same script as the stage-② gate: the measurement and the thing that fails on a new one are
one derivation, so they cannot drift apart.

**No second AST walker was written.** `readOwnRegistrations` in
`scripts/unit-registry-collision.mjs` — objectui#7134's walker, the one the dispatch named —
was factored into a new export `readRegistrationClaims` that returns the CLAIMANT (namespace,
`skipFallback`, `register` vs `registerLazy`, file, line) instead of only the key.
`readOwnRegistrations` is now a projection of it at the default options, so objectui#7134's
gate reads exactly what it read before; its own suite (82 cases across three sibling gate
tests) passes unchanged.

The half that is not readable from a call site — `registerAllFields()` walks a map, the
placeholder registrar walks an array — comes from `INDIRECT_REGISTRATIONS` and
`deriveRegistryKeys` in `scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs`, the table
`regenerate-known-schema-types.mjs` already follows. 129 of the 425 claims arrive that way.

**⭐ The predicate is DISTINCT FULL TYPES, not "more than one registration."** A console lazy
stub and its plugin both claiming one bare key under the SAME full type is this repository's
normal shape — the shape objectui#6416 converged `plugin-report` onto, and the reason
`report-bare-key-ownership.test.ts` replays in both orders. Such a key has one owner by
construction, whichever phase a host observes. Counting registrations would have reported all
thirty of those as defects.

### Three instrument defects, all found and all reported rather than quietly corrected

The card names two from the originating run. Neither can reach this instrument, and a third
one was found here — in the same family, and in the direction that manufactures findings.

1. **Bare type-NAME attribution pooling** — structurally absent: nothing here is attributed by
   a type's NAME. A claim's identity is the call site plus the key name, so two registrations
   in one file at different lines are two claims.
2. **An unbuilt tree resolves to `any`** — structurally absent: this derivation asks no type
   checker and reads no `.d.ts`. ⚠️ But running it on both trees found the NEIGHBOUR of that
   defect and it was real: the population was **1633 files unbuilt and 1639 built**, the six
   being `apps/site/.next`, `apps/site/.source` and a generated `plugin.d.ts`. A population
   that moves with whether someone has built is one no two runs agree on. Fixed by excluding
   dot-segments and emitted declaration files; the population is now 1622 and **zero of its
   files are git-ignored** (lit control: the same `git check-ignore` call returns
   `apps/site/next-env.d.ts` and does not return `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts`).
3. **⭐ NEW — a `.tsx` source parsed as plain TS silently loses the registration's meta
   object.** The inherited walker created every source file with `ScriptKind.TS`. In a `.tsx`
   renderer the JSX in the inline component argument swallows the rest of the argument list,
   so the meta literal is simply not there — and a call carrying `skipFallback: true` reads as
   a bare-name CLAIMANT. Measured on `ui:calendar`: before the fix the sweep reported **three**
   contested keys, two of them (`calendar`, `calendar-view`) pure artefacts of the mis-parse.
   Inert for objectui#7134's own population, which holds **zero** `.tsx` files — pinned.

### Lit controls, both directions — the gate fails if either goes dark

|---|---|---|
| must be VISIBLE as already-solved | `text` · `image` · `avatar` · `html` · `grid` (the five `FIELD_TYPES_SKIP_FALLBACK` names) and `line_items` | all six come back as `skipFallback` stand-downs |
| must be VISIBLE as live-but-agreed | `object-map`, `object-kanban` — two claimants each, ONE full type | both visible, correctly not reported |
| must not be empty | five FLOORS over every population the verdict rests on | all cleared |

## The one contested bare key: `dashboard`

| claimant | full type | skipFallback | via |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apps/console` — `apps/console/src/preview-gallery.tsx:36` | `plugin-dashboard:dashboard` | no | `registerLazy` |
| `apps/console` — `apps/console/src/register-plugins.ts:65` | `plugin-dashboard:dashboard` | no | `registerLazy` |
| `packages/plugin-dashboard` — `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/index.tsx:79` | `view:dashboard` | no | `register` |

⭐ **This is the objectui#6416 shape, still live, and it is on neither inherited list.** Bare
`dashboard` declares namespace `plugin-dashboard` before the chunk loads and `view` after it —
"which answer a host got depended on when it asked".

⚠️ **And the second objectui#6416 consequence follows too, unmeasured until now.**
`register()` clears the lazy stub for the type it registers, and the type it registers is
`view:dashboard` — so the `plugin-dashboard:dashboard` stub is never cleared: no component is
ever stored under it, `hasLazy` stays true forever, and `packages/cli/src/utils/known-schema-types.ts`
lists all three spellings (`dashboard`, `view:dashboard`, `plugin-dashboard:dashboard`) as
renderable. ⛔ Stated as a measurement, ⛔ not acted on — see the prohibition below.

⛔ **Not decided here.** Picking a spelling decides which declaration governs an authored
`{ "type": "dashboard" }` node. That is the same class of ruling objectui#9256 holds eleven
registrations for. The deliverable makes it decidable.

---

## ⚠️ What is NOT measured here

- **This is a SOURCE derivation, not a runtime one.** It reads registration call sites and two
  declared collections. A registration reached through a path none of that covers is invisible
  to it — which is why the three unresolvable sites are declared with their reasons instead of
  dropped, and why an undeclared one fails the gate.
- **Import order itself is not measured.** The verdict is "two declarations claim this name",
  not "declaration A wins today". Which one wins is the thing that depends on the host, and
  asserting today's answer is exactly what `report-bare-key-ownership.test.ts` warns cannot
  tell "declared" from "happened to be observed after the right step".
- **Test-body registrations are out of the population** on purpose: they happen when a test
  runs, in that worker's registry. objectui#7134's gate is the one that cares about those.
- **The `dashboard` unsatisfiable-stub consequence above is read off `Registry.register`'s own
  lazy-clearing lines**, not executed. It matches objectui#6416's measured shape; it has not
  been re-measured in a live registry here.

Stage ② (the gate, its shrink-only ledger and the full ablation) is in the draft pull request
that follows this comment.
